fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. At Patara they find a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, so they board it and set sail (Acts 21:2). Notice how simple it is. They find a ship, board it and set sail.
Macedonia is a fair guess, friend, and I get why it came to mind. But the text says the ship at Patara is crossing over to Phoenicia (Acts 21:2). Macedonia isn't on this ticket.
Soldiers would make this a very different trip. The text says the ship was to unload its cargo at Tyre (Acts 21:3). Soldiers aren't mentioned in these verses.
Horses on a boat? I'd pay to see that, but the text doesn't show it. The ship was at Tyre to unload its cargo (Acts 21:3). The text names cargo, not horses.
Right on, baker. Through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to go up to Jerusalem (Acts 21:4). Notice the word "kept." This wasn't a one-time comment.

You got it, baker. The disciples, with their wives and children, knelt down on the beach to pray with Paul's crew (Acts 21:5). That's a whole crowd of disciples on their knees in the sand. No fancy stage needed.
There's no letter in this scene, friend. The text says the disciples knelt down on the beach to pray with them (Acts 21:5). Ephesus doesn't come up in these verses.

Yes, baker. Agabus, a prophet who came down from Judea, took Paul's belt, bound his own feet and hands, and spoke about the owner of that belt (Acts 21:11). He didn't leave any doubt about who the message was for. That's a message you can see before you even hear it.

Philip, the evangelist whose home they were staying in, is a good guess since the scene is at his house. But the text says Agabus took Paul's belt (Acts 21:11). Philip isn't the one whose belt Agabus takes.

The Philistines are a real group in the Bible, so I see why they came to mind. But Agabus says the belt's owner will be handed over "…to the Gentiles." (Acts 21:11) That's the group named in the prophecy.
Correct, baker. Paul answers, "Why are you weeping and breaking my heart?" (Acts 21:13) The people were pleading with him, and I think it really did hit him in the heart. That's a tender moment.

Yes, baker. Paul says, "I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus." (Acts 21:13) That's a man who has made up his mind, and he says exactly what he's ready for and who it's for. Verse 14 says he would not be dissuaded (Acts 21:14).

Slipping away isn't in Paul's answer at all. He says, "I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus." (Acts 21:13) Being bound and dying are what he names.

That's right, baker. Some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied them to Jerusalem (Acts 21:16). They took them to stay at the home of Mnason the Cypriot, an early disciple (Acts 21:16). That's a good friend's kind of company.
The elders from Ephesus don't appear in these verses, friend. The text says some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied Paul's crew (Acts 21:16). That's the group that goes along.
